strategy_spec.name: single_node_tp
strategy_spec.description: Single-node tensor parallel. Splits the model across all local GPUs. TP size is set to the GPU count at deploy time. The simplest multi-GPU strategy — works for all model architectures.

guide:
## Overview

[Step-5 Preview](https://huggingface.co/stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview) is a multimodal
MoE model with hybrid sparse/sliding-window attention, a 1M-token context window,
and multi-token prediction (MTP).

The [NVFP4 checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview-NVFP4)
is available through the NVFP4 variant below.

## Docker

```bash
docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:step-5-preview

docker run --rm -it \
    --gpus all \
    --ipc=host \
    --network=host \
    --volume "$HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface" \
    --entrypoint /bin/bash \
    vllm/vllm-openai:step-5-preview
```

Run the following commands inside the container. Model access is required;
use `hf auth login` if the checkpoint requires authentication.

## FP8: single node on 4 B300 GPUs

The examples use four B300 GPUs. Choose TP4, TEP4, or DEP4:

| Mode | Tensor parallel | Data parallel | Expert parallel |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP4 | 4 | 1 | Disabled |
| TEP4 | 4 | 1 | 4 |
| DEP4 | 1 | 4 | 4 |

```bash
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3
```

On Blackwell, TEP4 and DEP4 use MegaMoE. TP4 uses the default MoE backend
because MegaMoE requires expert parallelism.

For FP8 on H200, use eight GPUs: TP8, TEP8, or DEP8, respectively.
Set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7` and change the parallel size
from 4 to 8 (DEP keeps TP=1). Omit the MegaMoE flag on Hopper.

These are separate layouts: TP4 and TEP4 use DP=1; DEP4 uses TP=1.
`--max-num-seqs` applies per DP rank. The 1M-token context limit includes
input and output; reduce `--max-model-len` or concurrency if KV cache memory
is insufficient.

## NVFP4: single node on 4 B300 GPUs

Use [stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview-NVFP4)
with the same Step-5 image. The checkpoint includes both NVFP4 and BF16 layers;
quantization is detected from its config.

```bash
docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:step-5-preview

docker run --rm -it \
    --gpus 4 \
    --ipc=host \
    --network=host \
    --volume "$HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface" \
    --entrypoint /bin/bash \
    vllm/vllm-openai:step-5-preview
```

Inside the container, reuse one of the TP4, TEP4, or DEP4 commands above,
replacing the checkpoint with `stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview-NVFP4` and setting
`--max-model-len 320000`.
Keep `--reasoning-parser step5` and `--tool-call-parser step5` unchanged.

| Mode | Parallel arguments |
| --- | --- |
| TP4 | `--tensor-parallel-size 4` |
| TEP4 | `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` |
| DEP4 | `--tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` |

TP4 uses automatic MoE backend selection for the mixed-precision layers.
TEP4 and DEP4 use MegaMoE for routed experts; shared experts run separately.
Send requests with `"model": "stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview-NVFP4"`.

Available context and concurrency depend on the remaining KV cache memory.

## Send a request

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data '{
      "model": "stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview",
      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
      "max_tokens": 4096,
      "stream": true
    }'
```
